messages:
jess: Hi all, first-day snag. I upgraded my company MacBook Pro to macOS Monterey 12.6 overnight and now it won't boot to the login screenit shows an Apple folder with a question mark. When I boot into Recovery it shows \"MDM: Not enrolled\" and Kandji isn't there. Who handles revived/re-enrolls and data rescue? @it-support
onboard-bot: Welcome to Redwood, @jess! :tada: IT will help with revive/re-enroll. Pinging now.
it-support: Hey Jess, sorry you hit this. Quick triage: are you on Apple Silicon or Intel? Can you paste the output of these when in Recovery Terminal: `diskutil apfs list`, `fdesetup status`, `profiles status -type enrollment`? Also did you do a Migration Assistant restore or a fresh upgrade?
jess: I'm on Apple Silicon (M1). I can get to Recovery -> Utilities -> Terminal. Ran the commands, outputs below:
```
$ diskutil apfs list
APFS Container (1 found)
+-- Container disk1
    +-- Physical Store disk0s2
    +-- APFS Volume Macintosh HD
       Mounted: /
       APFS Volume Disk (Role): disk1s1 (Preboot)
$ fdesetup status
FileVault is On.
$ profiles status -type enrollment
No mobile device management enrollment found.
```
I did an in-place upgrade from Big Sur earlier today (no Migration Assistant).
mika: This looks like the firmware update part of the Monterey upgrade may have been interrupted, leaving the system in a partially non-bootable state and MDM profile not applied. For Apple Silicon a proper "revive" via Apple Configurator (another Mac + USB-C cable) will reinstall the firmware and restore the OS while keeping the internal drive. If you can't access a spare Mac, we usually either ship a loaner + Configurator kit or ask the user to bring the device to the office.
it-support: Two immediate options: (A) if you have a Time Machine or iCloud backup we can provision a loaner and restore your data there while we revive the original, or (B) we ship a Configurator kit/loaner to you overnight and do the revive remotely. We won't ask you to enter corporate credentials until it's re-enrolled. Which works for you?
sec-ops: Security note: do not plug in any USB installers from unverified sources and don't enter SSO credentials while the device shows "MDM: Not enrolled." We'll require the device be revived and re-enrolled before we allow VPN/SSO. If we ship hardware, we'll require signature and encrypted courier.
people-ops: Welcome Jess! If you want us to ship, DM your preferred shipping address and phone number and we'll coordinate with IT for overnight. We'll also expedite a temporary loaner so you can continue onboarding.
jess: I don't have another Mac. Please ship the kit/loaner. DMing address now. Quick Q: is there anything I can try locally to avoid shipping?
it-support: On Apple Silicon there's not much that fixes a partial firmware/OS state from Recovery alone. Avoid Disk Utility erase for now. If you have an iPhone and a second Mac we could do a revive; otherwise shipping is safest. We'll open a ticket and mark it high priority since this blocks onboarding.
jess: DM sent. Appreciate the quick responses.
it-support: Ticket created, shipping loaner + Apple Configurator kit overnight. We'll schedule a remote session during the revive; the process will reinstall firmware and the OS but should preserve your APFS container unless we instruct otherwise. After revive we'll push Kandji targeted re-enroll and escrow a new FileVault recovery key.
sec-ops: We'll monitor the device during revive and ensure the new recovery key is escrowed to the company KMS and logged. Also logging a short note to block SSO until re-enrolled.
people-ops: Loaner tracking and instruction email sent. Enjoy your first week and let us know if you need any checklist changes while you wait.
jess: Thanks everyone 60a I'll be online on the loaner once it arrives. Appreciate the help and the warm welcome!
